question: As a Stellar asset issuer, can I charge transfer fees, cap supply, or freeze a holder, and what is actually possible at the protocol level?

golden.answer: Classic assets have no protocol per-transfer issuer fee and no max-supply field. An issuer caps supply operationally by locking the issuing account after issuance; a SAC admin moved away from the issuer can still mint. An issuer can freeze a holder by deauthorizing the trustline when AUTH_REVOCABLE is set. Custom transfer logic needs a Soroban token.
keyFacts: Classic assets have no protocol per-transfer issuer fee hook.
Classic assets have no protocol max-supply field.
Locking the issuing account stops further issuance of the classic asset.
Deauthorizing a trustline freezes a holder when the revocable flag is set.
avoid: Do NOT claim that classic Stellar assets have a built-in issuer transfer tax or an immutable max-supply field.
golden.notes: A SAC admin moved with set_admin can still mint after the issuer is locked; do not penalize an answer that adds this.

sources.note: SAC mint requires the current admin's auth; set_admin can move the admin away from the issuer.

corroboration.claim: As of 2026-08-29, classic Stellar Assets have no built-in per-transfer issuer-fee hook; transfer-fee logic requires a contract token.

evidence.note: The official comparison says contract tokens provide transfer fees that are not available in Stellar Assets.
The full classic operation list has payment, path-payment, offer, set-options, trustline, and clawback operations, with no issuer-fee operation.
AccountEntry and TrustLineEntry expose balances, limits, authorization flags, and extensions, but no per-transfer issuer-fee field.

corroboration.claim: As of 2026-08-29, classic Stellar Assets have no immutable max-supply field; issuers limit supply by locking issuance authority.

evidence.note: The official guide limits supply by setting the issuing account's master weight to zero after issuance.
AccountEntry and TrustLineEntry have no max-supply or total-supply member.
The SAC design rationale says total supply is unavailable because Stellar Classic does not support it.

corroboration.claim: Locking the issuing account caps classic supply only while any deployed SAC's admin is still the issuer; a SAC admin moved with set_admin can still mint.
